entries.text: The `Core\Response` methods that send a body now start with `send`: `sendJson`, `sendHtml`, `sendText`, `sendBytes` and `sendSlotted`. `startStream` starts a streamed response. The old names were `json`, `html`, `text`, `bytes`, `slotted` and `stream`.
entries.instead: Write `Core\Response::sendJson($data)` where you wrote `Core\Response::json($data)`, and the same for the other five methods.

entries.text: `Core\Request::queryParameter`, `queryParameters` and `queryParametersAs` read the query string. `formField`, `formFields` and `formFieldsAs` read a submitted form. The old names were `query`, `queryArray`, `queryAs`, `post`, `postArray` and `postAs`.
entries.instead: Write `Core\Request::queryParameter('page')` where you wrote `Core\Request::query('page')`, and `Core\Request::formField('email')` where you wrote `Core\Request::post('email')`.

entries.text: `Core\Sse::startStream` starts an event stream, and `setRetryDelay` sets how long a browser waits before it connects again. The old names were `stream` and `retry`.
entries.instead: Write `Core\Sse::startStream()` where you wrote `Core\Sse::stream()`, and `$stream->setRetryDelay($after)` where you wrote `$stream->retry($after)`.

entries.text: `Core\Metrics::setGauge` sets the value of a gauge. The old name was `gauge`.
entries.instead: Write `Core\Metrics::setGauge(...)` where you wrote `Core\Metrics::gauge(...)`.

entries.text: `Core\Task::runAfterResponse` runs a function after the response is sent. The old name was `afterResponse`.
entries.instead: Write `Core\Task::runAfterResponse(...)` where you wrote `Core\Task::afterResponse(...)`.

entries.text: `Core\Router\Match` reads the values of a route with `parameters()` and `parameter($name)`. The old names were `params` and `param`.
entries.instead: Write `$match->parameter('id')` where you wrote `$match->param('id')`.

entries.text: `Core\Script::arguments()` returns the value a script was started with. The option of a spawned script's `with()` is now `arguments:` too. The old name was `args` in both places.
entries.instead: Write `Core\Script::arguments()` and `with(arguments: ...)` where you wrote `Core\Script::args()` and `with(args: ...)`.

entries.text: The `Core\Cli` methods that prompt or draw now say so: `askSecret`, `showLive`, `showProgress` and `selectMany`. The old names were `secret`, `live`, `progress` and `multiSelect`.
entries.instead: Write `Core\Cli::askSecret(...)` where you wrote `Core\Cli::secret(...)`, and the same for the other three methods.

entries.text: `Core\Test::answerCli` gives the answers for the prompts of a test. `Core\Test\Outcome->hasPassed()` checks whether a test passed. The old names were `scriptAnswers` and `passed`.
entries.instead: Write `Core\Test::answerCli([...])` where you wrote `Core\Test::scriptAnswers([...])`, and `$outcome->hasPassed()` where you wrote `$outcome->passed()`.

entries.text: Every `Core\Xml\Writer` method that writes a part of the document now starts with `write`. For example, `writeText` writes text and `writeAttribute` writes an attribute. The old names were `content`, `attribute`, `comment`, `cdata`, `instruction` and `doctype`.
entries.instead: Write `$writer->writeText('...')` where you wrote `$writer->content('...')`, and add `write` to the other five method names.

entries.text: `Core\IO` writes the word "directory" in full: `createTemporaryDirectory`, `makeDirectory`, `removeDirectory` and `isDirectory`. `Core\IO::metadata` returns the `Core\IO\Metadata` of a file. The old names were `temporaryDir`, `makeDir`, `removeDir`, `isDir` and `stat`.
entries.instead: Write `Core\IO::makeDirectory($path)` where you wrote `Core\IO::makeDir($path)`, and `Core\IO::metadata($path)` where you wrote `Core\IO::stat($path)`.

entries.text: `Core\Path::parent` returns the folder of a path, and `Core\Path::fileName` returns its last part. `fromWorkingDirectory` and `thisDirectory` write their words in full. The old names were `dirname`, `basename`, `fromCwd` and `thisDir`.
entries.instead: Write `Core\Path::parent($path)` where you wrote `Core\Path::dirname($path)`, and `Core\Path::fileName($path)` where you wrote `Core\Path::basename($path)`.

entries.text: Each `Core\BigInt` method that computes a new number is named for its result: `plus`, `minus`, `multipliedBy`, `dividedBy`, `remainder`, `raisedTo`, `raisedToModulo`, `negated`, `shiftedLeft` and `shiftedRight`. The old names were `add`, `sub`, `mul`, `div`, `mod`, `pow`, `powMod`, `neg`, `shl` and `shr`.
entries.instead: Write `$a->plus($b)` where you wrote `$a->add($b)`, and the same for the other nine methods.

entries.text: `Core\Decimal::divideExact`, `divideRounded` and `power` write their words in full. The old names were `divExact`, `divRound` and `pow`.
entries.instead: Write `Core\Decimal::divideRounded(...)` where you wrote `Core\Decimal::divRound(...)`, and the same for the other two.

entries.text: `Core\Math::quotient` divides two whole numbers, `divide` divides two floats, and `remainder` returns what is left after a division. The old names were `intDiv`, `fdiv` and `mod`.
entries.instead: Write `Core\Math::quotient($a, $b)` where you wrote `Core\Math::intDiv($a, $b)`, and the same for the other two.

entries.text: `Core\Arr::difference` and `Core\Arr::intersection` compare two arrays. `Core\Arr::groupCounts` counts the elements of each group. The old names were `diff`, `intersect` and `countBy`.
entries.instead: Write `Core\Arr::difference($a, $b)` where you wrote `Core\Arr::diff($a, $b)`, and the same for the other two.

entries.text: `Core\ObjectSet->intersection()` and `difference()` return a new set. The old names were `intersect` and `diff`.
entries.instead: Write `$a->intersection($b)` where you wrote `$a->intersect($b)`, and `$a->difference($b)` where you wrote `$a->diff($b)`.

entries.text: `Core\Uri->resolved()` and `signed()` return a new address and leave the original unchanged. The old names were `resolve` and `sign`.
entries.instead: Write `$base->resolved($link)` where you wrote `$base->resolve($link)`, and `$uri->signed(...)` where you wrote `$uri->sign(...)`.

entries.text: `Core\Time\DateTime->nanoseconds()` and `Core\Time\TimeOfDay->nanoseconds()` return the part of the second in nanoseconds. The option of `with()` is `nanoseconds` too. The old name was `nanos` in both places.
entries.instead: Write `$time->nanoseconds()` and `with(nanoseconds: ...)` where you wrote `$time->nanos()` and `with(nanos: ...)`.

entries.text: `queryEach` and `queryEachAs` run a query and read its rows one at a time. `runTransaction` runs a function in a transaction, and `Core\Db\Column->isNullable()` checks a column. The old names were `stream`, `streamAs`, `transaction` and `nullable`.
entries.instead: Write `$db->queryEach(...)` where you wrote `$db->stream(...)`, and `$db->runTransaction(...)` where you wrote `$db->transaction(...)`.

entries.text: `Core\Http\Client::openStream` opens a streamed request, and `Core\Http\TlsInfo->isVerified()` checks the certificate. The old names were `stream` and `verified`.
entries.instead: Write `Core\Http\Client::openStream(...)` where you wrote `Core\Http\Client::stream(...)`, and `$tls->isVerified()` where you wrote `$tls->verified()`.

entries.text: `Core\Ldap\Connection->hasValue()` checks whether an entry has a value, and `searchChanges()` reads the entries that changed. `Core\Ldap\Filter::approximately` builds an approximate match. The old names were `compare`, `changes` and `approx`.
entries.instead: Write `$ldap->hasValue(...)` where you wrote `$ldap->compare(...)`, and the same for the other two.

entries.text: Every `Core\Ldap\Ad\AccountFlags` method that checks a flag now starts with `is`, `has`, `allows` or `uses`, for example `isDisabled()` and `hasNonExpiringPassword()`. The field `trustedToAuthForDelegation` of `with()` is now `trustedToAuthenticateForDelegation`.
entries.instead: Write `$flags->isDisabled()` where you wrote `$flags->disabled()`. The page of `Core\Ldap\Ad\AccountFlags` lists every new name.

entries.text: Every `Core\Ldap\Ad\GroupType` method that checks a flag now starts with `is`, for example `isGlobal()` and `isSecurityGroup()`. The old names were `system`, `global`, `domainLocal`, `universal`, `appBasic`, `appQuery` and `security`.
entries.instead: Write `$type->isGlobal()` where you wrote `$type->global()`, and the same for the other six methods.

entries.text: `Core\RateLimit::consumeLocally` counts a request in the memory of this server process. `Core\RateLimit\Decision->isAllowed()` checks the result. The old names were `shed` and `allowed`.
entries.instead: Write `Core\RateLimit::consumeLocally(...)` where you wrote `Core\RateLimit::shed(...)`, and `$decision->isAllowed()` where you wrote `$decision->allowed()`.

entries.text: `Core\WebPush\Sent->isGone()` checks whether the browser removed the subscription. The old name was `gone`.
entries.instead: Write `$sent->isGone()` where you wrote `$sent->gone()`.

entries.text: The option `cwd` of `Core\Process::run` and `Core\Process::spawn` is now `workingDirectory`. The option `args` of `Core\Queue::push` is now `arguments`.
entries.instead: Write `{ workingDirectory: '...' }` where you wrote `{ cwd: '...' }`, and `{ arguments: [...] }` where you wrote `{ args: [...] }`.

entries.text: Each `Novis\Image\Image` method that returns a new image is named for it, for example `resized()`, `blurred()` and `withText()`. `keepingMetadata()` replaces `metadata({ keep: true })`, and `encodeVariants()` replaces `variants()`. `Image::compare` returns a `Comparison` with the property `differenceImage`, which was `Diff` with `diff`.
entries.instead: Write `$image->resized(width: 800)` where you wrote `$image->resize(width: 800)`. The page of `Novis\Image\Image` lists every new name.

entries.text: Each `Novis\Pdf\Document` method that returns a new document now starts with `with`, for example `withHeader()` and `withPassword()`. `created()` is now `withCreationTime()`.
entries.instead: Write `$document->withHeader(...)` where you wrote `$document->header(...)`, and add `with` to the other method names.

entries.text: Each `Novis\Spreadsheet\Sheet` and `Workbook` method that adds to the file says what it adds, for example `addRow()`, `addChart()` and `addSheet()`. `setPrintOptions()` replaces `print()`. `Chart->withSeries()` and `combinedWith()` return a new chart.
entries.instead: Write `$sheet->addRow([...])` where you wrote `$sheet->add([...])`. The pages of `Sheet`, `Workbook` and `Chart` list every new name.

entries.text: A `#[Core\Json\Derive]` class with a property of a `Core` class such as `Core\Time\Date` or `Core\Uuid` stopped the program with an internal error. It is now the compile error `E0756` at that property, because only `Core\Time\Instant` has a JSON form. For the others, declare the property `string` and convert the text after the decode.
`nvs agent show` prints the help of a built-in name. For an enum of `Novis\Image`, `Novis\Intl`, `Novis\Pdf` or `Novis\Spreadsheet`, it now also lists the enum's cases.

When a request calls `Core\Response::sendFile` more than once, each call replaces the earlier file. The request sends only the last file. The `max_output` limit in `nvs.toml` now counts only that file.

`Core\Str::afterPrefix` checks that a string starts with a prefix and returns the rest of the string. `Core\Str::beforeSuffix` does the same at the end. Both return `null` when the string does not match.

The warning `W1036` shows a `Core\Str::slice` that cuts off a prefix or a suffix after `Core\Str::startsWith` or `Core\Str::endsWith` tested it. It names `Core\Str::afterPrefix` or `Core\Str::beforeSuffix`, which do both in one call. When the cut is the first line inside the `if`, the editor offers a fix that writes the call for you.

`Core\Str::startsWith`, `Core\Str::endsWith` and `Core\Str::replaceAll` find a match only where it does not split a character. So `Core\Str::startsWith("e\u{301}", "e")` is `false`, because the accent belongs to the `e`. The pair `"\r\n"` is one character, so `"\r"` alone does not match inside it.
entries.instead:
To change Windows line ends with `Core\Str::replaceAll`, put the pair first: `["
" => "
", "" => ""]`. To check whether a line ends with a line break, check for `"
"` and for `"
"`.

entries.text: `Core\Str::trim`, `Core\Str::trimStart` and `Core\Str::trimEnd` remove whole characters. A character at the end is removed only when the `characters` option has every code point of it. So `Core\Str::trim("e\u{301}", { characters: "\u{301}" })` returns the text unchanged, because the accent belongs to the `e`.
entries.instead: To remove a letter with its accent, put every code point of it in `characters`, such as `"e\u{301}"`.

entries.text: You can pass `Foo::class` where a `class<T>` is expected. You do not need to write `as class<T>`. A class name in a string variable still needs `as`.

`Core\Config::set` changes only the settings on one list, and the page of `Core\Config::set` shows the list. A name you write in the call that is not on the list gives the error `E0667`. A template string that no name on the list fits gives the warning `W1037`.
entries.instead: Remove each call that sets a name not on the list. Such a call cannot change anything.

entries.text: The page of each setting says whether a request may change it with `Core\Config::set`. A page for a block lists the settings in it that a request may change.

Code in a package (a library your program installs) may change only `[limits]` settings. If code in a package writes another setting name in a call to `Core\Config::set` or `Core\Config::restore`, the call gives the error `E0667`.
entries.instead: Remove the call. In a package, it cannot change anything.

entries.text: Inside the name you pass to `Core\Config::set` or `Core\Config::restore`, the editor lists the settings a request may change. The hover on a name says how a request may change that setting.

After an edit, the editor checks fewer files. A change inside a method body or a comment checks only the file you edit. A change to a method also checks the subclasses, and for a `public` method the files that call it.

`Instant::toIso` writes a year before year 1 with four digits, such as `-9999-01-02T01:59:59Z`. `Instant::fromIso` reads this text back. JSON reads an `Instant` with the same rules as `Instant::fromIso`.
entries.instead: Read a year before year 1 as four digits after the `-`.

entries.text: In the VS Code Explorer, a file that declares one attribute shows the letter `A`. Its tooltip is "This file declares an attribute."
Inside `#[Name(`, the editor shows the fields of the attribute declaration as signature help. Each field shows its doc comment.
An attribute that nothing declares has the quick fix **Declare the attribute**. It writes an `attribute` declaration in the same file, with a field for each key you wrote.
The editor colours the words `class`, `method`, `property` and `parameter` after `on` in an attribute declaration. Each field name has the colour of a property name.
The outline lists each attribute declaration and its fields. The body of an attribute declaration folds.
The editor completes `attribute` and `repeatable` at file level and in a class or interface body. It also completes the type of each field in an attribute declaration.
Go to definition, find references, highlight and rename work on the fields of an attribute declaration. They also work on each key in a `#[Name(key: …)]` use.
`nvs code order` moves an attribute declaration in a class to the top of the class, with the `enum` and `type` declarations. **Order class members** in the editor does the same.

`Core\Csrf::token` saves no session data for a new visitor. The response still sends the session cookie, and the server accepts the token on the next request. The server saves session data only when the program writes a value with `Core\Session`.

Every use of a revoked object (an object after a call to its `revoke()` method) throws `RevokedObjectError`. This includes `.=` on a property, an `inout` property argument, a call of a method reference and `isinit`. It also includes a conversion to a string, a comparison, a `foreach`, a delegated method and a `static` call through the object.

Some decoders take a type, such as `Core\Json::decodeAs` and `Core\Request::jsonAs`. They check every class inside a shape or an array of that type, at any depth. `Core\Request::jsonAs`, `queryAs` and `postAs` give the error `E0810` when such a class has a plain `string` property.
entries.instead: Write `tainted string` on each string property of a class that a request decoder reads.

entries.text: `Core\Uri::encodeComponent` throws a `LogicError` when its argument is exactly `.` or `..`. In a path, such a segment changes which resource the URI names.
entries.instead: Check the value before you encode it. For a query value, use `Core\Uri::withQueryParameter` or `Core\Uri::buildQuery`.

entries.text: The output of a child process is `tainted bytes`. The version text of a database server and the name an LDAP server returns are `tainted string`. Another program or a server writes this text, so it may contain input from outside.
entries.instead: Write `tainted` on the variable that keeps the value. Before the value goes into a path, a query or a command, convert it with a check such as `as ?int`. Or use the method that makes it safe there.

entries.text: `Throwable::$message` is `tainted string`, because some error messages contain input text. The text of a `Core\Ldap\Filter` and of a `Core\Ldap\Dn` is `tainted string` too.
entries.instead: Write `tainted string` on a variable that keeps an error message or the text of a filter or a DN.

entries.text: `Image::encode`, the pixels of `Image::raw`, each file of `Image::variants` and the result of `Pages::merge` are `tainted bytes`. An image or a PDF file may be an upload. `Font::fromBytes` takes `tainted bytes`.
entries.instead: Write `tainted bytes` on the variable that keeps the result. A response body, a file and storage all take `tainted bytes`.

entries.text: `Core\Bytes::at` takes `tainted bytes` and returns a plain `uint`. `Core\Bytes::join` takes an `array<tainted bytes>`, and the result is then `tainted bytes`.

Text from a `Core` method is `tainted` unless the method says where the text comes from. A `tainted` value may reach a parameter that does not take it. The error then names the method that makes the value safe for that parameter.
Each task that `Core\Task::all` runs has the same capabilities and the same memory limit as the code that calls it. A task that needs more memory than the limit does not get it.
`Core\Serialize::decode` gives a revocable object that is in no collection. Encoded data cannot change which collections contain a revocable object. Data that tries throws a `ParseError`.
entries.instead: Encode the objects again with `Core\Serialize::encode`.

entries.text: When the memory limit stops a `set`, `add` or `push`, the revocable object is not added, and a later `revoke()` works as usual. `Core\Debug::dump` does not print a `#revocable` line.

A `[[restrict]]` rule covers every use of a class or method: a union type, `static::NAME`, a default value, an attribute argument and a route link. A package can restrict only its own code and the code in `Core`. A rule for any other code gives the error `E0665`.
entries.instead: Move a restriction on another package's code into that package, or into your application's `package.toml`.

entries.text: `nvs reload` exits with `1` when a server does not reply. Its line says `could not be reached` or `closed the connection without a reply`. A server that is shutting down prints a line that says it is stopping.

In development, the server checks the `Host` header of every request from a proxy on this machine. This check does not use `X-Forwarded-For`. The `421` response has a text body that names the host to add to `development_hosts` in the `[server]` block.
entries.instead: Add the host name your local proxy sends to `[server] development_hosts`.

entries.text: The methods this entry names throw a `LogicError` in a request, a connection, a scheduled task and a queued job. They work in a test, and in a request or a program that a test starts. They also work in a command-line program.
entries.instead: Call these methods only in a test or in a command-line program.

entries.text: A request to the test server uses the test's clock and its `env:` variables. What the request logs or sends as mail is in `Core\Test::logs` and `Core\Test::sentMail`.
A file that a response sends with `Core\Response::sendFile` counts toward the test's memory limit. A file that does not fit ends the test with a memory error.
A double can replace an interface method that has a body with a function. The double then runs that function.
`nvs test --since` also runs the tests that reach a deleted or renamed file or method. When it cannot tell which tests a change affects, it runs every test.

The three epoch methods round down to the earlier whole unit. For example, the instant half a second before 1970 gives `-1` seconds. `Instant::fromEpoch` with the result and the remaining part gives the same instant.
entries.instead: Before 1970, add one to the result when the instant has a part of a unit left.

entries.text: `Instant::fromIso` reads an upper-case `T` and `Z`, a `.` before the fraction, and an offset with a colon, such as `+02:00`. A lower-case `t` or `z`, a comma, the second `60` or an offset like `+0100` throws a `ParseError`. So does a year that does not have four digits, such as `-009999`.
entries.instead: Write `T`, `Z`, a `.` before the fraction, and an offset with a colon, such as `+01:00`.

entries.text: `Date::fromIso('-0000-01-01')` throws a `ParseError`. Year 0 is written `0000`.
entries.instead: Write year 0 as `0000`.

entries.text: `Zone::of` gives the zone the name the time-zone database uses. `Zone::of('europe/berlin')` gives the zone `Europe/Berlin`.
The parameters of `Date::at` are named `year`, `month` and `day`.
entries.instead: Write `Date::at(year: 2024, month: 12, day: 24)`.

entries.text: `Core\Arr::append` uses the same key as `$a[] = $v`. After `unset` removes the largest number key, the next value gets the key after the removed one.
entries.instead: To number the keys again from `0`, call `Core\Arr::values` first.
